title: Hook Call Order: Unconditional Hooks
prompt:
React relies on hooks being called in the same order on every render -- conditional hooks break that contract. **Requirements:** 1. Import `useEffect` and `useState` from `react`. 2. Export a function component `Greeting({ visible, name })` with props `visible: boolean` and `name: string`. 3. Declare ALL hooks at the top level, unconditionally. 4. Track a `greeting` state derived from `name`. 5. Use `useEffect([name])` to set `greeting` to `Hello, ${name}`. 6. Do the conditional rendering AFTER the hooks: when `!visible`, return `null`; otherwise render `

{greeting}

`. This pattern avoids the `Rendered fewer hooks than expected` runtime error.
hints: Every `useState`, `useEffect`, `useReducer` call must happen on every render in the same order.
Do early returns AFTER the hooks are declared, not before.
If some logic is only needed sometimes, conditionally branch inside the hook callback -- not the call site.

Greeting.tsx.description: Call useState at the top level
Call useEffect at the top level
